name: Tafjord ski trek — steep-ground exposure and fall-line constraint

method.objective: Minimize horizontal ground distance on terrain slope >15 degrees; compare supported distance/maximum-grade tradeoffs. Below 10 degrees, no heading constraint.
method.heading_rule: For slope s > 10 degrees: absolute deviation from uphill OR downhill fall line <= 30 - s degrees.
method.search: Direction-aware weighted shortest paths: cost = distance_above_15 + lambda*total_distance, with terrain caps 20,22.5,25,29.9 and sampled lambda values. These are candidate Pareto options, not a certified global resource-constrained optimum.
method.grid: Terrarium z13, ~8.9 m latitude-corrected cells; 176 primitive travel directions, exact segment/cell clipping. Corner-touching cells must satisfy the cap; positive-length intersections must satisfy the heading rule. Long flat-region moves may use a shorter direction stencil.
method.day1_under20: No path found within the 25 km reachable domain using 176 or 640 directions under a 20-degree cap. A 33.373 km sub-20-degree candidate was found with a larger search domain and is diagnostic only.
method.validation: Independent Python re-integration of every positive-length segment/cell intersection; all heading-rule excesses <0 degrees. Coordinates retain double precision to preserve tight heading margins.
method.scope: Terrain-only model; snow, ice, avalanche exposure and obstacles not modeled.
